name: Game HUD
tagline: Readable version of the in-game layer: sharp corner, tabular number, single signal color and state-oriented hierarchy.
feeling: controlled voltage, "everything is just a click away"
best: in-game layers, esports broadcast panel, live score screen, control panel
avoid: long reading text, form-heavy corporate streams
signature: **Sharp corner:** 2/4px; The HUD acts like a frame, no smooth rounding.
**Single signal color:** accent only live status and primary action; A second neon hue is prohibited.
**Tabular digit:** score/timer/counter mono and right aligned; digit width does not jump.
**Thin accent edge:** cards are separated by a 1px accent 22% edge, no shadow is used.
**Uppercase title:** title and tag uppercase; body text remains in sentence order.
must: Accent number one; Status information is also given via text or icon.
All numbers are written with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.
Card and button corner ≤ 4px; 1px border is used instead of shadow.
HUD layer up to 3 levels: ground, panel, floating notification.
mustNot: Infinite flashing indicator or animated score (v6 out of scope).
More than three status colors; arbitrary use of the yellow/green/red trio.

essence: Game HUD is built on the assumption that every number the player sees on the screen is tied to a decision moment: score, health, duration and target are aligned on the same grid. No ornaments; There is contrast and sharpness.
origin: Arcade cockpits, console HUDs and PC game menus; After the 2010s, esports became simpler with broadcast panels.
brief: Design an in-game control panel. Score, health and time are on the same horizontal strip; main action single button. Numbers are mono and tabular, corners are 2px, accent is only for live state. No ornaments, shadows and animations; The hierarchy comes from the point size.

name: Game Racing
tagline: Interface in speedometer language: narrow digits, warm accent, beveled cut and racing telemetry hierarchy.
best: racing game menus, telemetry panel, sports broadcast graphic
avoid: calm corporate form flows, long reading screens
a11y: medium (warm accent safe in large print)
signature: **Bevel crop:** 8–12px diagonal crop instead of corner; The button and the card share the same cutting angle.
**Night figure:** Rajdhani's tight width keeps the score and runs count in one line.
**Hot accent:** orange only speed/ranking accent; cold blue is not used as a second color.
**Telemetry strip:** horizontal bars labeled thin and mono; It reads like an indicator, not a chart.
**Racing typography:** header uppercase and wide tracking, body 15px quiet.
must: The card and button cutout are cropped to the same diagonal angle (8–12px).
Accent is used only for speed, ranking and primary action.
All numeric fields mono or narrow display; decimal aligned.
Strip indicators are 6px high, background is `--surface-2`.
mustNot: Animated speedometer or scrolling telemetry (v6 out of scope).

refs.label: Rajdhani (Google Fonts)
refs.use: narrow display; number and title family

essence: Game Racing brings the display logic of the racing cockpit into the interface: each number is a decision (brake, gear, row) and each decision must be read at a glance.
origin: Racing game menus, motorsport broadcast graphics and analog instrument panels.
brief: Design racing game menu: lap, qualifying and time in the same lane; cards are cross-cut; accent orange only emphasis on speed. The numbers are tight and taboo. No animation, no flourishes.
